document_check.note: The document is Gao H, Zhao S, Zheng G, et al. 'Using a dual-stream attention neural network to characterize mild cognitive impairment based on retinal images', Computers in Biology and Medicine 166 (2023) 107411. It is a multimodal (fundus plus OCT) deep-learning study of MCI, matching the review's 'retinal multimodal deep learning (Gao et al. 2023)'.

cited_result: The review cites the study as an example of retinal multimodal deep learning without a number, so the principal result is appraised. This is the classification performance of the dual-stream cross-fusion attention network (DuCAN), using paired fundus photographs and OCT images to classify MCI, AD and cognitively normal participants in the first (Daping Hospital) dataset: accuracy 91.64%, AUC 96.78%, MCI precision 84.96% (Table 2).
tool_reason: The cited result is the diagnostic classification performance of a deep-learning model (MCI against AD and controls), so PROBAST with PROBAST+AI considerations applies.

domains.rationale: The first dataset is a case-control sample of diagnosed AD and MCI hospital patients and age-matched controls, with small numbers. No recruitment procedure or ocular exclusion criteria are reported, and the authors acknowledge that coexisting eye disease was not addressed.

domains.rationale: There are only 29 MCI participants. Data are split and counted at image level (18 OCT images per eye, both eyes, randomly paired images) with no statement of participant-level splitting, so the same person is likely on both sides of the split. Loss weights and hyperparameters were chosen on validation performance. Class imbalance and the missing fundus images were not properly handled. There is no calibration and no external validation of the MCI classifier. The reported results are internally inconsistent.

overall_rationale: The participants domain is high: this is a small hospital case-control sample (29 MCI) with no ocular exclusions. The analysis domain is high: data were handled at image level with no participant-level split reported (likely same-person leakage), tuning used validation performance, there was no external validation or calibration, and the reported results are inconsistent. The predictors and outcome domains are unclear. The 91.64% accuracy is at high risk of being optimistic.

applicability.rationale: Diagnosed hospital AD/MCI patients against age-matched controls, while the model is intended for community screening.
Swept-source OCT and fundus imaging suit eye-care settings, but acquisition consistency across groups and sources is not reported.
NIA-AA 2011 clinical diagnosis for the first dataset matches the review's MCI target condition.
